author: c2-sql-sme-critic (independent PostgreSQL SME critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; rechecked commit f18bccaf)

findings.claim: Answer leakage introduced in GIFT item 'o3 no ELSE': the stem now asks what a CASE with no ELSE returns when no WHEN is true, and appends '(When ELSE is left out, PostgreSQL behaves as if ELSE NULL had been written.)'. That parenthesis is the answer, so the keyed option '=NULL' needs no recall. The added sentence is true (9.19.1), but it leaves the item testing nothing.

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): 9.19.1 CASE: "If the ELSE clause is omitted and no condition is true, the result is null."

findings.recommendation: Remove the parenthesis from the stem; if the item needs context, move that sentence into the correct option's feedback.

findings.claim: Broken item introduced in GIFT 'o1 present values': replacing the 'phone != NULL' distractor produced two identical options, '~NOT (phone \= NULL)' twice, with near-identical feedback. A four-option item now offers three distinct choices, and the not-equal-to-NULL misconception that the page's apply question and the earlier version tested (!= and <> with NULL are unknown) is no longer practised here.

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): 9.2: "Ordinary comparison operators yield null (signifying “unknown”), not true or false, when either input is null. For example, 7 = NULL yields null, as does 7 <> NULL"; "!= is an alias, which is converted to <> at a very early stage of parsing"

findings.recommendation: Restore a distinct distractor, for example the earlier one: ~phone != NULL with the feedback that any comparison with NULL, including !=, is unknown for every row.

items.note: The branch now reads "a value cannot be read as the type it needs. Check that every value in one column, or in one COALESCE or CASE, is the same kind", which matches 10.5 type resolution; verified that COALESCE(fee, 'Not priced') now gets this advice.
